fields.quote: Retry only retryable failures, within a fixed budget
fields.rationale: after throws when !error.retryable or attempt === retries (source after; functions.mjs). after.permanent.calls is 1 with error permanent; before.permanent.calls is 2. exhausted.calls is 3 when retries is 2, matching attempt <= retries. The title does not claim successful delivery or cross-invocation exclusion.
source.json title begins with "Cedar Relay: filter retries and increase delays".

fields.quote: Permanent failures stop immediately; retryable failures use increasing requested delays without a delivery deduplication guarantee.
fields.rationale: after.permanent: calls 1, delays [], error permanent. after.exhausted delays are [10, 20] from sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt), and contract 3 says delays are requested milliseconds. Contract 2 and duplicate.effects === 2 deny a deduplication guarantee. The dek describes the changed loop, not the old loop (before.permanent.calls === 2).

fields.quote: Fictional source change and deterministic modeled examples
fields.rationale: "deterministic modeled examples" matches probe-results.assumptions ("Deterministic modeled send outcomes and immediate sleep promises; no timing or production measurement"). Nothing in source.json, contracts, probe.mjs, or probe-results.json labels the source change as fictional. That word is not evidenced by the supplied inputs.

fields.quote: A rejected acknowledgment can still follow a committed remote effect.
fields.rationale: Contract 2: a send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits. The duplicate probe models effect: true with a retryable error, then a second effect; duplicate.effects is 2 for before and after. probe.mjs comments that case as a lost acknowledgment.
Organizational heading. It does not assert a checkable fact about the source, contracts, or probes.

fields.quote: The old loop retried every rejection
fields.rationale: before has no retryable check; it sleeps and continues until attempt === retries. before.permanent.calls is 2 after a non-retryable rejection. before.exhausted retries transients until the budget ends. "Every" is the classification policy (all rejections are retryable until the budget throws), not a claim that a zero budget still retries.

fields.quote: The old loop retried rejected sends until the retry budget ran out. It requested a ten-millisecond delay between attempts.
fields.rationale: before sleeps 10 after each failed send unless attempt === retries. before.exhausted: calls 3, delays [10, 10], error transient. Contract 3: delays are requested milliseconds. before.zeroBudget: calls 1, delays [] when retries is 0, so the budget can run out with no delay.
Organizational heading, not a checkable source or probe claim.
after inspects error.retryable before sleep. after.permanent delays are [] (stop with no wait). Retryable paths sleep only after that check fails to throw.

fields.quote: The changed loop stops on a non-retryable error. Otherwise it requests delays of 10, 20, then 40 milliseconds as the attempt index increases. A budget of two retries permits up to three sends. A rejected sleep prevents the next send.
fields.rationale: Stop-on-non-retryable is supported (after.permanent.calls === 1, delays []). Two retries → three sends is supported (attempt <= retries; after.exhausted.calls === 3). Sleep rejection preventing the next send is supported (after.sleepFailure.calls === 1, error sleep-failed; contract 3). The delay list is not: sleep runs only when retryable and attempt !== retries, so after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20], not [10, 20, 40]. 40 would be 10 * 2 ** 2 at attempt 2, which is the throw path when retries is 2. The same paragraph states that two-retry budget, so the 40 ms request is contradicted by the modeled trace, not merely unshown.
Organizational heading, not a checkable source or probe claim.

fields.quote: A retry can duplicate a remote effect
fields.rationale: Contract 2: no deduplication or idempotency. duplicate.effects is 2 for before and after (effect on the rejected send, then a second successful send).

fields.quote: The author describes exactly-once delivery, but the supplied contract permits a send to reject after its effect commits. The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects. Separate invocations share no retry budget or exclusion mechanism.
fields.rationale: source.body: the author says the change "makes delivery exactly once." Contract 2 permits reject-after-commit and supplies no deduplication. duplicate.effects === 2. Contract 4: separate calls share no retry counter and no lock or cross-call exclusion. concurrentCalls totals 2 effects from two invocations. These sentences report the author claim and then the contract/probe limits; they do not treat exactly-once as established.
Organizational heading, not a checkable source or probe claim.
after.permanent.calls is 1 versus before.permanent.calls of 2. Retryable exhausted paths still use three sends when retries is 2; the title limits the claim to permanent failures.

fields.quote: The change filters failures and increases requested delays. It bounds send attempts per invocation, not successful delivery or duplicate effects.
fields.rationale: after filters on error.retryable. after.exhausted delays [10, 20] versus before [10, 10]. Bounds are per call (attempt <= retries; contract 4). duplicate.effects remains 2; contract 2 supplies no delivery or idempotency guarantee. This does not treat the modeled traces as a universal delivery guarantee.

missing_material_limitations.limitation: Sleep is not requested on the throwing attempt, so 10 * 2 ** attempt is never passed to sleep when attempt === retries or the error is non-retryable.
missing_material_limitations.why_material: Section 1 states delays of 10, 20, then 40 as the attempt index increases in the same paragraph as a two-retry / three-send budget. The exhausted probe for that budget records only [10, 20]. Readers are not told the last attempt never waits.
sources: source after: await sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt) only after the retryable && attempt !== retries guard

missing_material_limitations.limitation: Requested delays are not measured wall-clock durations; probe sleeps resolve immediately with no timing or production measurement.
missing_material_limitations.why_material: Partly hedged by "requested" in the dek and section 1, but the 10/20/40 list still reads as durations the loop will wait. Contract 3 and probe-results.assumptions are the full limit.

reviewer_language_leakage.rationale: "Supplied contract" is audit-harness phrasing for source.json contracts, not reader-facing product language.

reviewer_language_leakage.quote: The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects.
reviewer_language_leakage.rationale: Names a modeled probe scenario in reviewer terms. The duplicate trace and probe.mjs comment support the two-effect fact, but the wording leaks the evaluation setup.

reviewer_language_leakage.quote: Fictional source change and deterministic modeled examples
reviewer_language_leakage.rationale: Methodology label for the audit packet rather than a reader-facing claim about Cedar Relay behavior. "Fictional" is also unevidenced (see /meta unsupported).

code_diagram_errors.quote: Otherwise it requests delays of 10, 20, then 40 milliseconds as the attempt index increases.
code_diagram_errors.error: The after formula is 10 * 2 ** attempt, which equals 10, 20, 40 at attempt 0, 1, 2, but sleep is skipped when attempt === retries. With the paragraph's budget of two retries, after.exhausted.delays is [10, 20]. No 40 is requested. There is no diagram; this is a prose mis-trace of the loop.

quotes: Otherwise it requests delays of 10, 20, then 40 milliseconds as the attempt index increases.
A budget of two retries permits up to three sends.
The modeled lost-acknowledgment example records two effects.
reader_facing_prose.rationale: Most body copy matches the after function and the modeled traces, and section 3 correctly refuses a delivery or uniqueness guarantee. The change section still states that the loop requests 10, 20, then 40 ms while also stating the two-retry budget whose exhausted probe records only [10, 20]. That is a reader-facing contradiction of exact modeled results, not an extra untested case. Reviewer phrasing in section 2 and meta also leaks into the prose. Passing traces (permanent stop, three sends, two duplicate effects, sleep failure) are not a reason to treat the 40 ms delay as observed.

unresolved_uncertainty: If "10, 20, then 40 milliseconds as the attempt index increases" is read only as the closed form of 10 * 2 ** attempt at indices 0–2, and not as sleeps actually requested under retries === 2, /sections/1/content could be scored supported with a missing-limitation note instead of contradicted. The next sentence names that two-retry budget, so this review treats the 40 ms request as contradicted.
"Fictional" in /meta has no source or probe witness. If meta is allowed as an unevidenced methodology label, some rubrics would mark it nonfactual instead of unsupported.
Section eyebrows are scored nonfactual as labels. If headings must be supported or unsupported, they would be unsupported as source claims because the contracts never use those labels.
